dct_description_sm: Each file includes the lake name, sampling date, depth, and represented ecoregion. Data are subdivided into categories, depending on their nature or sampling techniques. Separate files present (1) spectral properties of dissolved organic matter and nutrient concentrations, (2) concentrations of dissolved anions and cations, (3) concentrations of dissolved greenhouse gases (including CO2, CH4, and N2O), (4) characterisation of particulate organic matter (chlorophyll-a and fatty acids), (5) characterisation of surface sediment organic matter (lignin and fatty acid content), and (6) sedimentation rates with surface sediment carbon and nitrogen content. Additionally, algal counts are available for the northern boreal forest lakes.

23 lakes were sampled during the summers of 2021 (southern Saskatchewan) and 2022 (northern Saskatchewan and Victoria Island, Nunavut) following a south-north ecogeographical gradient from the prairies through boreal forest into tundra, with objective to better understand how terrestrial ecogeography affects lake’s biogeochemistry. The dataset includes characterisation of dissolved and particulate fractions of organic matter from the lakes’ water columns (i.e., DOC, nutrients, dissolved ions, chlorophyll-a, fatty acid composition, spectral characteristics of DOM, as well as dissolved greenhouse gas concentrations), and surface sediments (lignin content and fatty acids) together with sedimentation rates.
dct_title_s: Biogeochemical characteristics of lakes along a south-north gradient: from the prairies to tundra [Western Canada]
